question.worked_solution:
The cross-product rule states that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}c\times f(t)\,\text{d}t=c\times {\int }_{0}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Applying the cross-product rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}c\times f(t)\,\text{d}t & =c\times {\int }_{0}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(-i+j)\times (16\,i+8\,j+2\,k) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 16 & 8 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 8 & 2\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 16 & 2\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 16 & 8\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(2-0)i-(-2-0)j+(-8-16)k \\  & =2i+2j-24k.\end{aligned}
$$
